rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Figs. 6-9, Tables S1-S6 - a three-season (2018-2020) field experiment in a 2.1 ha young almond orchard in Hellin, Spain, with five treatments in three randomized blocks, combining Sentinel-2 NDVI/SAVI time-series with pressure-chamber stem water potential and tree-dimension measurements.
rows.notes: The study reports its own results that severe sustained deficit irrigation (33% ETc) lowered NDVI/SAVI, stem water potential and tree dimensions by about 13%, 23% and 14% relative to full irrigation, and that moderate deficit (67% ETc) did not differ from control (Sections 3.1-3.2, Conclusion). This supports only the detection/diagnosis step: the study did not define any operational thresholds, did not use the indices to adjust irrigation scheduling, and did not measure yield or yield losses, so the claimed crop-production effect (threshold-based scheduling that prevents yield losses) is not tested. The authors moreover state (Discussion) that NDVI/SAVI showed only a low correlation with <U+03A8>stem (results not shown) and are limited for identifying short-term variations in plant water status, which weakens the 'precise diagnosis' wording. Because the study establishes a precondition (detection of severe deficit via VIs and <U+03A8>stem) rather than the claimed effect, Q2 is no and upstream is set. Uncertainty exists for the detection result itself (standard-error bars in Figs. 6-9) and the authors note the 10 m Sentinel-2 resolution limitation for heterogeneous canopies, but these cannot count given Q2 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a primary field experiment on young almond with sentinel-2 VIs, stem water potential and tree dimensions; it reports no yield data and no irrigation-scheduling thresholds. The neighbouring context sentence (ground cover increasing vigour 19-42% and 'reducing soil structural degradation by 7-8%') misreads the study, which reports a 7-8% reduction in trunk perimeter under vegetation cover, not soil degradation.
